outcome: Oracle extraction preserves durability, provenance and recovery semantics across process boundaries and migration: manifest-protected artifact reads, stable source refs, validation failures and durable Backend→QA continuation remain correct after package ownership changes.
currentProblem: Oracle behavior matured through manifest validation and durable Backend→QA continuation while still colocated. Moving code without reconciling these durability/provenance seams risks silently weakening accepted-artifact identity, crash recovery, or compatibility even if simple resolver tests still pass.
constraints: Physical extraction must not weaken producer/revision/acceptance/content-digest checks for manifest-protected artifacts.
Durable Backend→QA continuation must persist and recover the exact refs it already relies on.
Default direct-reader behavior remains supported unless explicitly superseded by accepted research.
Migration cannot fabricate provenance or silently reinterpret missing durable state.
Compatibility shims, if needed, are temporary and have explicit removal/closure criteria.
successCriteria: Research identifies every durability/provenance seam crossing the new package boundary.
Manifest-protected QA reads remain fail-closed on identity/provenance/content mismatch.
Fresh-process Backend→QA continuation resolves the same accepted artifact refs after extraction.
Existing direct-reader callers either continue unchanged or have an explicit bounded migration path.
Failure/recovery evidence is sufficient to detect semantic regressions that package-level unit tests would miss.
